intro: What you owe suppliers and how it gets paid: their bills, checked against what you ordered and received, what falls due and when, and the payments that settle them. Nothing is posted to your books until a bill is approved and posted.
start: Check each supplier's payment terms, so their bills fall due on the right day.
Enter your first bill, or press Bill it on a receipt, then submit and post it.
Open What is due each week and pay what falls due with Pay suppliers.
Look at Held bills now and then, so nothing stays stuck.

Nothing is posted until it is submitted and approved. With an approval policy, press Approve, or wait for the approver.
The bill is matched against what was received. If it matches, it is posted and owed; if not, it is held and shows on Held bills.

articles.after: The bill shows the three-way match line by line: what was ordered, received and billed, and any price difference.
tips: Someone other than the person who entered or submitted the bill posts it, unless an approval policy covers posting.
The same supplier invoice number cannot be entered twice for one supplier.
Freight, duty or clearing on goods you received can be added to what those goods cost, instead of booked as an expense.
